basic_details.job_title: AAI Advisor Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online for 14 Posts
basic_details.short_information: Airports Authority of India (AAI) is engaging 14 Advisors on contract in its ATM (Air Traffic Management) Directorate under Advertisement No. 15/2026/CHQ/AD, open only to retired Air Traffic Controller Officers (ATCOs). Applications go by email to [email protected] and must be received on or before 30 November 2026; submission opens on 14 November 2026. The age limit is a maximum of 65 years as on 30 November 2026.

The selected person must undergo a medical examination at his/her own cost and submit the medical fitness certificate at the time of joining. In the normal course one month's notice is given, and the Advisor can also seek termination by giving one month's notice. Advisors must be of good character and integrity. AAI reserves the right to shortlist or reject candidature without assigning any reason.

content_sections.heading: About Airports Authority of India
content_sections.text: Airports Authority of India is a Government of India Public Sector Enterprise constituted by an Act of Parliament. The notice says it is responsible for creating, upgrading, maintaining and managing civil aviation infrastructure on the ground and in the air space of the country, and that it holds Mini Ratna Category-1 status. Its office is at Rajiv Gandhi Bhawan, Safdarjung Airport, New Delhi-110003.

content_sections.heading: AAI Advisors Job Description
content_sections.text: The notice lists the following duties for each post code. Each also includes any other task assigned by the concerned ED (post codes 01 to 09) or the concerned GM (post codes 10 and 11). Post 01 (CAP): critical regulatory functions of licensing, training oversight and DGCA compliance, and timely disposal of regulatory matters. Post 02 (ATFM): training and capacity building, documentation, operational advisory services, ATFM system enhancement, international best practices and future technologies, future concept development, technical evaluation and system upgradation, interoperability and system integration, and stakeholder coordination. Post 03 (Survey & Carto): supervising the OLS Survey at airports (existing and proposed), water aerodromes and heliports; collecting vital data and critical obstacles and surfaces; checking DGPS results; assuring data quality in compliance with DGCA CAR and preparing FPD data; guiding GIS analysts on ICAO and DGCA survey requirements; supervising airport base maps, approach charts, vertical significance charts, OFZ charts and other charts; use of datums and colours such as True North and EGM-08; survey operations, data quality assurance and evaluation of obstacles. Post 04 (ASM): specialized airspace planning, route design and coordination with defence agencies. Post 05 (FPD): timely execution of procedure design and associated regulatory activities. Post 06 (ATS): CNS/ATM and PPP airport agreements, and coordination with stakeholders for meteorological services. Post 07 (SAR): critical SAR functions, including updation of SAR manuals, execution of SAR agreements, and conduct of training and exercises. Post 08 (HRD/TRG): ATM manpower planning, training oversight at ATSTO, long term training strategy, ATSTOs capacity building initiatives, and ensuring availability of competent ATCO manpower across AAI units. Post 09 (DoAS): processing of NOC/Appellate cases, stakeholder coordination, aeronautical assessments, and ensuring timely compliance with regulatory requirements related to airport infrastructure projects. Post 10 (CSMIA): INDRA Automation, airspace management, operational coordination and stakeholder liaison; and, for the future expansion of Navi Mumbai International airport, its traffic growth, coordination between nearby airports and management of complex airspace operations. Post 11 (RHQ Western Region): operational policy matters advice, strategic planning, regulatory compliance, coordination with field units, and implementation of ATM initiatives.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Application in the prescribed format (Annexure-I), duly filled in. Self-attested copy of proof of age (10th Certificate/Passport). Self-attested copies of educational qualification documents. Self-attested copies of work experience documents. The Annexure-I form also carries a photo box and the applicant's signature and declaration. All of the above must be combined in one PDF of not more than 5 MB.

faq.question: Q1. How many Advisor posts has AAI announced in 2026?
faq.answer: AAI has announced 14 Advisor posts on contract in its ATM Directorate across 11 post codes. Post codes 05, 09 and 10 have 2 posts each; the other eight post codes have 1 post each.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for AAI Advisor?
faq.answer: The application must be sent by email on or before 30 November 2026. Submission opens on 14 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. Who can apply for AAI Advisor posts?
faq.answer: Air Traffic Controller Officers retired from Central/State Government in Pay Matrix Level-15 and above (7th CPC), or retired CPSE employees at E-7 level and above (3rd PRC) or equivalent. They must also have the Air Traffic Control experience stated for the post code.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for AAI Advisor?
faq.answer: The maximum age is 65 years as on 30.11.2026, the last date for receiving applications.

faq.question: Q5. What is the monthly remuneration of an AAI Advisor?
faq.answer: Monthly remuneration is 50% of the last Basic Pay Drawn (Basic Salary + Dearness Allowance). The notice does not print a rupee amount for it.

faq.question: Q6. Are transport and mobile charges paid on top of the remuneration?
faq.answer: Yes. Transportation charges up to Rs.40,000 per month (Central/State Government/E-8 and above) or up to Rs.30,000 per month (E-7 level) are payable on claim basis, or AAI transport is provided. Broadband and mobile charges are Rs.1,500 or Rs.1,000 per month respectively, on claim basis.

faq.question: Q7. How do I apply for the AAI Advisor post?
faq.answer: Fill in the Annexure-I application, attach self-attested documents, combine them in a single PDF of not more than 5 MB and email it to [email protected] by 30 November 2026. Any other mode of application will not be accepted.

faq.question: Q8. How are AAI Advisors selected?
faq.answer: Only shortlisted applicants are called for application verification and interview. Selection is based on the merit ranking of the interview.

faq.question: Q9. Is the AAI Advisor job permanent?
faq.answer: No, it is a contract engagement. The initial tenure is 11 months, and either AAI or the Advisor can end the contract with one month's notice in the normal course.

faq.question: Q10. Will AAI pay TA/DA for attending the interview?
faq.answer: No. The notice says no TA/DA will be paid for attending application verification or interview, or for joining the assignment or on its completion.
